title: Findings from Trial of Using Speed-tracking Devices for Heavy Vehicles
what_it_is: Findings from Trial of Using Speed-tracking Devices for Heavy Vehicles

sections.label: Speed-tracking device trial for heavy vehicles
sections.summary: TP requires speed limiters for heavy vehicles and trialled speed-tracking devices from December 2017 to August 2018, finding them accurate but tamper-prone.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Today, the Traffic Police (TP) already require the use of speed limiters for heavy vehicles.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Between December 2017 and August 2018, TP conducted a trial on speed-tracking devices, to assess if they might be more effective than speed limiters in discouraging heavy vehicle drivers from speeding.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: TP concluded from the trial that even though the speed-tracking devices were accurate in measuring vehicle speed, they were also susceptible to being tampered with.

sections.label: Speed tracking devices not mandatory
sections.summary: TP has decided not to make the speed tracking devices mandatory.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: TP has decided not to make the speed tracking devices mandatory.

sections.label: First-time offenders' penalties
sections.summary: First-time offenders are liable for up to three months' imprisonment, a $1,000 fine, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: First-time offenders are liable for an imprisonment term of up to three months, a fine of $1,000 or both.

sections.label: Increased composition sums for speeding
sections.summary: MHA announced higher composition sums from 1 April 2019, raising the sum for heavy vehicle drivers exceeding the speed limit by over 31 kilometres per hour from $200 to $400.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: MHA recently announced increases in composition sums for road traffic offences which will take effect on 1 April 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: With this change, the composition sum for heavy vehicle drivers who exceed the speed limit by over 31 kilometres per hour would be increased from $200 today to $400.

sections.label: Decrease in heavy vehicle speeding violations
sections.summary: Between 2014 and 2018, speeding violations involving heavy vehicles with speed limiters decreased by about 37%, from 1,737 in 2014 to 1,087 in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: Between 2014 and 2018, the number of speeding violations involving heavy vehicles with speed limiters actually decreased by about 37%, from 1,737 in 2014 to 1,087 in 2018.
